# Native wrapper (Capacitor 8): architecture and open items

**Status:** scaffolded 2026-10-28 on `feature/accounts`; generated by Claude Sonnet 5.5 via Claude Code at T.P's request. **Human review required.** Not built or run on any device or emulator: the machine had no JDK, Android SDK or macOS. Addresses the "no native wrapper" gap (row 1) of the [store-readiness audit](store-readiness-audit-2026-10-28.md); human steps are in [NATIVE.md](../../apps/plan-b-mvp/web/NATIVE.md).

## Architecture

- `apps/plan-b-mvp/web/` stays the Vite + React shell. `capacitor.config.ts` (appId `au.reroute.app`, a placeholder to confirm; `webDir: dist`; Android scheme `https`, iOS scheme `reroute`) packages `dist` into `android/` and `ios/`.
- The legacy `app.js`, `offline.js`, `app.css`, icons and vendor files are normally served by Flask next to `dist`. `scripts/prepare-native.mjs` copies them into `dist` for the bundle. `sw.js` is not bundled (WKWebView custom schemes cannot run service workers; registration already has a `.catch`).
- The app calls `fetch("/api/...")`. `src/native/api.js` rewrites those to `VITE_API_BASE` on native only (build-time, set by `npm run build:native`).
- `src/main.jsx` calls `initNative()` only when `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()`. Every adapter in `src/native/` is a dynamic import, so the browser never downloads them. Measured: main chunk 124.20 to 124.37 kB gzip (+0.17 kB). Browser checked at 390x844: no console errors, no native chunk requested, geolocation untouched.
- Capacitor 8 uses Swift Package Manager for iOS (`ios/App/CapApp-SPM`), so CocoaPods is not needed. `cap add ios` worked on Windows; building needs a Mac.

## Adapters (`web/src/native/`)

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `platform.js` | `isNative()`, `platform()`; the only eager file |
| `index.js` | startup, adds `native` classes to `<html>`, loads the others |
| `api.js` | relative `/api` to `VITE_API_BASE` |
| `geolocation.js` | replaces `navigator.geolocation` and the geolocation permission query with `@capacitor/geolocation` (native prompt; `app.js` unchanged) |
| `network.js` | re-dispatches `online`/`offline` window events from `@capacitor/network` (feeds the existing offline banner) |
| `deeplinks.js` | `appUrlOpen` for `https://<domain>/...` and `reroute://...` to the router (history + `popstate`), closes the in-app browser (OAuth return), Android back button; emits `reroute:deeplink` |
| `share.js` | `navigator.share` to the native share sheet (the existing "Share with other apps" button then appears and works) |
| `chrome.js` | status bar style and colour follow `data-theme`, Android edge-to-edge overlay, hides the native splash, iOS keyboard accessory bar off |
| `push.js` | wired to the trip "Watch in the background" toggle: our priming sheet, then the OS prompt, then the FCM token to `/api/push/native-register`; foreground toast, tap routing, badge reset (see Push below) |
| `auth.js` | `signIn("apple" or "google", cfg)` via `@capgo/capacitor-social-login`; **not wired**: the accounts screen owner calls it and sends the `idToken` to the server |

Haptics: `src/haptics.js` already routed to `@capacitor/haptics` (light/medium/heavy impact, selection, error notification) when native and to `navigator.vibrate` on the web; unchanged. The optional iOS-Safari `<input switch>` tick was skipped (undocumented trick, not needed in the native shell).

## Plugins and why

app (deep links, back), browser (OAuth in-app browser), geolocation, haptics, push-notifications (APNs/FCM; audit blocker 5), network, share, splash-screen, status-bar, keyboard. (`@capacitor/local-notifications`, `@capacitor/preferences` and `@capacitor/device` were installed but never imported; removed and `npx cap sync` re-run on 2026-10-28. The bearer token now uses `@aparajita/capacitor-secure-storage`, see Hardening notes.), `@capgo/capacitor-social-login` 8.7.5 (Apple and Google in one maintained plugin, peer `@capacitor/core >=8`; `@codetrix-studio/capacitor-google-auth` only supports Capacitor 6 and `@capacitor-community/apple-sign-in` 7+, so neither was used). `@capacitor/filesystem` not needed. Dev: `@capacitor/cli`, `@capacitor/assets`, `sharp`, `typescript` (needed to read `capacitor.config.ts`). Remove unused plugins before release to shrink the permission surface if a reviewer asks.

## Platform config

- **Android:** compile/target SDK 36, min SDK 24 (Capacitor template). Permissions: INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, ACCESS_COARSE/FINE_LOCATION, POST_NOTIFICATIONS, VIBRATE. No background location (navigation runs in the foreground; if added later it needs a Play declaration and a prominent disclosure). `usesCleartextTraffic=false`, `network_security_config.xml` (HTTPS, system CAs), `allowBackup=false`. App Links intent filter with `autoVerify` for `reroute.example` (TODO real domain) and the `reroute://` scheme. Adaptive icon, mipmaps and splash generated from `favicon.svg`.
- **iOS:** deployment target 15. `Info.plist`: `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`, `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption=false`, `reroute` URL scheme. `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`: no tracking; collected data precise location (not linked), email, name, user ID and device ID (push token) linked, all for app functionality; required-reason APIs UserDefaults CA92.1, FileTimestamp C617.1, SystemBootTime 35F9.1, DiskSpace E174.1. `App.entitlements`: `aps-environment`, `applinks:reroute.example` (TODO), Sign in with Apple. These need a paid Apple Developer team; delete the keys to test on a free personal team. The files were wired into `project.pbxproj` by hand: open the project once in Xcode and confirm they appear in the App target.
- **Safe areas:** `viewport-fit=cover` is set and `app.css` pads with `env(safe-area-inset-*)` on the header, scroll areas, footers and sheets. Android 15+ edge-to-edge relies on the status-bar overlay plus those insets; confirm the top inset on a real Android 15 device.

## Contracts for the server owner (not implemented here; `server.py` untouched)

1. **CORS:** allow origins `https://localhost` (Android) and `reroute://localhost` (iOS), methods GET/POST/OPTIONS, headers `Content-Type` and `Authorization`. If sessions use cookies, they need `SameSite=None; Secure` and may still be dropped by WKWebView; prefer bearer tokens for native.
2. **(Implemented, see Push below)** `POST /api/push/native-register`, body `{"token": "<fcm or apns token>", "platform": "ios" | "android", "watch": <same object as /api/push/subscribe, or null>}`; return `200 {"ok": true}`, `400` on bad input; rate-limit like `/api/push/subscribe`. Sending via FCM HTTP v1 for both platforms (upload the APNs key to Firebase) is simplest. Add an unregister endpoint for logout.
3. **`/.well-known/assetlinks.json`** (`application/json`, no redirect):

```json
[{"relation": ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls"], "target": {"namespace": "android_app", "package_name": "au.reroute.app", "sha256_cert_fingerprints": ["<SHA-256 of the Play App Signing certificate; add the upload key for sideloaded tests>"]}}]
```

4. **`/.well-known/apple-app-site-association`** (served as `application/json`, no file extension, no redirect):

```json
{"applinks": {"details": [{"appIDs": ["<TEAM_ID>.au.reroute.app"], "components": [{"/": "/*"}]}]}, "webcredentials": {"apps": ["<TEAM_ID>.au.reroute.app"]}}
```

5. OAuth return: redirect the in-app browser to `https://<domain>/auth/callback?...` (App Link) or `reroute://auth/callback?...`; `deeplinks.js` maps both to the same path.

## Push (FCM for Android and iOS)

**Server** (`push_native.py`, `push.py`): Firebase Cloud Messaging HTTP v1 for both platforms, the same disruption monitor and watch as Web Push. Direct APNs is not implemented (upload the APNs key to Firebase instead). The OAuth token is signed with `cryptography`, so no `google-auth` dependency.

- `POST /api/push/native-register` `{token, platform: "ios"|"android", app_version, locale, watch|null}` returns `{ok, id}`; the `id` is what notification links (`/?alternatives=<id>`) carry. Requires JSON, an allowed `Origin`, and the `X-Reroute-Device` header (16 to 64 chars of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`; a custom header forces a CORS preflight, which is what makes the cookie-less native call CSRF-safe). Rate limited like `/api/push/subscribe`. Tied to the account when a session cookie or bearer token is sent. `503` JSON when FCM is not configured. Re-registering a token replaces its watch.
- `POST /api/push/native-unregister` `{token}`.
- FCM `UNREGISTERED` or `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (and HTTP 404) delete the token. Deleting an account deletes its tokens (`Accounts.on_delete`). Tokens are never logged. Storage: `data/push.json`, with the Web Push subscriptions.
- Env (secrets, never committed): `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` or `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE`.

**Client**: the trip "Watch in the background" toggle calls `window.rerouteNativePush.enable(watch, primeSheet)`. When permission is "prompt" the app sheet "Get disruption alerts?" shows first; "Not now" (or closing it) leaves everything working and does not use the one-time iOS prompt. "Denied" shows how to turn Notifications on in the phone's Settings. Android 13+ `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is requested by `requestPermissions()` after the sheet. In the foreground Android shows an in-app toast (iOS shows the system banner via `presentationOptions`); tapping a notification opens `/?alternatives=<id>` through the deep-link adapter; delivered notifications and the badge are cleared when the app opens. `push_enabled` is sent only with analytics consent.

**Set-up (human)**
1. Firebase console: create a project. Add an Android app (`au.reroute.app`) and an iOS app (same bundle id). Put `google-services.json` in `web/android/app/` and `GoogleService-Info.plist` in `web/ios/App/App/` (add it to the App target in Xcode).
2. Apple Developer: create an APNs Auth Key (.p8), then in Firebase Project settings, Cloud Messaging, Apple app configuration, upload it with the Key ID and Team ID.
3. Firebase Project settings, Service accounts, Generate new private key. Give the JSON to the server as `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE` (path) or `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`. Never commit it.
4. Server CORS must list `https://localhost` and `reroute://localhost` (`PLANB_CORS_ORIGINS`); `X-Reroute-Device` is already an allowed header.
5. Test: Android, `adb install` the debug build, enable alerts on a trip, then use Settings, Demo mode, "Send test disruption push"; test tap routing with `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "reroute://localhost/?alternatives=ID"`. iOS needs a real device and an Xcode or TestFlight build with the Push Notifications capability; simulators do not receive FCM.

## Hardening notes (2026-10-28 final fix pass)

- **Bearer token storage.** The native token is stored with `@aparajita/capacitor-secure-storage` 8.0.1 (Capacitor 8, maintained; iOS Keychain, Android Keystore-backed; `npm view` showed it modified 2026-09-23), through `web/src/native/tokenStore.js`, lazy-loaded only when `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()`. iCloud Keychain sync is off (`sync=false`). The web still uses the session cookie and never loads the plugin. An old `localStorage` token is moved on first read; if the plugin throws, the token falls back to `localStorage` so sign-in still works (a weaker, documented fallback). `npx cap sync` was run and the Gradle/SPM plugin lists committed. Not tested on a device. Re-check the iOS privacy manifest at archive time in case the plugin adds a required-reason API.
- **`UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities`** is now `arm64` (was the template's `armv7`).
- **`aps-environment`** stays `development` in `App.entitlements` on purpose. For App Store/TestFlight builds Xcode re-signs with the distribution profile, whose `aps-environment` is `production`; to make it explicit, in Xcode add a second entitlements file (`App.Release.entitlements` with `production`) and set it as `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS` for the Release configuration only. Needs Xcode and a paid team, so not done here; push tokens from a development build do not work against the production APNs endpoint and vice versa (`push_native.py` must be pointed at the matching APNs host/key).
- **R8/minification.** `minifyEnabled false` is unchanged because no Android SDK is available here to build and run a release. `android/app/proguard-rules.pro` now carries the Capacitor rules (plugin classes and `@PluginMethod`s, `@JavascriptInterface`, the app package, the plugins in use, line numbers for stack traces). **Enable R8 after a signed release build test:** (1) set `minifyEnabled true` (and `shrinkResources true`) in the `release` block of `app/build.gradle`; (2) `./gradlew bundleRelease` with the upload keystore; (3) install the resulting build on a real device (a Play internal-testing install of the AAB is best) and exercise sign-in (Google), push registration, location, share, haptics, the offline area and sign-out; (4) read `adb logcat` for `ClassNotFoundException` / `NoSuchMethodException` and add a `-keep` for each; (5) keep `app/build/outputs/mapping/release/mapping.txt` for every uploaded build (Play Console accepts it for deobfuscation). Only then ship it.
- **Domain.** `node scripts/set-domain.mjs --domain <host> [--dry-run]` rewrites the Android App Links host, the iOS associated domain and the `capacitor.config.ts` API host default; `python placeholders.py [--strict]` lists what is left.

## Still needs a Mac, accounts or secrets

Build and run on iOS (Mac, Xcode); Apple Developer Program (US$99) for signing, push, Associated Domains, Sign in with Apple and TestFlight; Google Play developer account (US$25) and upload keystore; Firebase project with `google-services.json` and `GoogleService-Info.plist`; production domain and the well-known files; Google Maps keys per platform (the web key is HTTP-referrer restricted and the bundled origin is `https://localhost` / `reroute://localhost`, so add those referrers or use a native-only key; audit row 8); Google and Apple OAuth client IDs; on-device testing of every adapter; screenshots, listing text, privacy labels and the Data safety form.

## Known limits

- `watchPosition` ids are shim-local; `maximumAge` caching is whatever the plugin does.
- Service worker features (offline shell, web push) are off in the bundle; offline maps use IndexedDB and still work.
- `allowNavigation` in `capacitor.config.ts` reads `VITE_API_BASE` at `cap sync` time; keep it set when syncing.
- Social login needs real client IDs; unused until wired.
